definitions.explanation: White cotton gloves with a knitted texture, commonly used for manual labor and gardening.

examples.japanese: ⟦{草|くさ}むしり→草むしり：08195_kusamushiri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{軍手|ぐんて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はめた。
examples.english: I put on work gloves to pull weeds.

examples.japanese: {軍手|ぐんて}なし⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{作業|さぎょう}→作業：02775_sagyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{汚|よご}れる→汚れる：01293_yogoreru⟧。
examples.english: If you work without gloves, your hands will get dirty.
Work gloves are handy when moving house.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{軍手|ぐんて} originally meant "military gloves" (⟦{軍|ぐん}→軍：02677_gun⟧ = military + ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧ = hand), as they were once standard issue for the Japanese military. Now they are everyday work gloves.

USAGE:
{軍手|ぐんて} are inexpensive, disposable cotton gloves sold in packs. Common uses include:
- ⟦{庭仕事|にわしごと}→庭仕事：20710_niwashigoto⟧ (gardening)
- {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し (moving)
- ⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧ (cleaning)
- DIY⟦{作業|さぎょう}→作業：02775_sagyou⟧ (DIY work)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {軍手|ぐんて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はめる (to put on work gloves)
- {軍手|ぐんて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧ (to take off work gloves)

COUNTER: {双|そう} or ⟦{組|くみ}→組：02668_kumi⟧ (for pairs)
